title: Discovery Marathon 2026 Review: Cebu's SRP Waterfront 42K
seo_title: Discovery Marathon 2026 Review | Cebu Philippines Race
meta_description: The Discovery Marathon 2026: September 20 at City Di Mare, Cebu City. 42K, 21K, 12K, 6K from KNC at the South Road Properties — registration pending.
dek: Set for 20 September 2026 at City Di Mare in Cebu's South Road Properties, this KNC-organised marathon offers unusual distances including 12K and 6K options. Registration pending.
verdict: The Discovery Marathon arrives in Cebu with a genuinely distinctive distance spread: a full marathon (42K), half marathon (21K), 12K, and 6K. That 12K in particular — sitting between the standard 10K and the half — is a rarity in Philippine road racing and gives intermediate runners a meaningful step-up option. Organised by KNC (the team behind Dagan Cebu), the race anchors at City Di Mare, a waterfront development in Cebu's South Road Properties (SRP), which offers wide, flat roads and sea breezes along the Cebu Strait. September in Cebu is transitional — the southwest monsoon is winding down and morning temperatures, while warm, are manageable with the coastal airflow. On the downside, registration is still pending as of this review, and KNC remains a mid-tier organiser in a market where production values vary considerably. For Cebu-based runners wanting a full marathon with distinctive distance options and an SRP waterfront setting, this is one to bookmark.

sections.heading: SRP: Cebu's Waterfront Running Corridor
paragraphs: Cebu's South Road Properties is a 300-hectare reclaimed waterfront development stretching along the Cebu Strait — wide, flat roads with minimal elevation change and consistent sea breezes that knock a degree or two off the tropical heat. [1] City Di Mare anchors the race as a modern, well-venued hub with parking and pre-race facilities. For a Cebu marathon, the SRP course is about as fast as it gets: no hill climbs, open sightlines, and the Cebu skyline as backdrop. The trade-off is limited shade — runners in the back half of the marathon field will feel the late-morning sun.

The Philippines doesn't have a Wikipedia-style 'climate of the Philippines' page per city, but Cebu's September pattern is well-documented: average highs around 31°C, morning lows of 25°C, and rainfall tapering as the southwest monsoon (habagat) gives way to the northeast monsoon (amihan). [2] [3] An early flag-off is essential, and runners should manage hydration carefully.

sections.heading: The Distance Spread: 12K and 6K Stand Out
paragraphs: Most Philippine road races run the standard 42K/21K/10K/5K menu. The Discovery Marathon swaps the 10K and 5K for a 12K and a 6K — a deliberate choice that changes who the race is for. [1] The 12K is a genuine intermediate distance: longer than a 10K tempo effort, shorter than a half-marathon training block. The 6K hits the sweet spot for runners graduating from 5K fun runs but not yet ready for a 10K race. It's a small detail, but it signals an organiser thinking about runner progression rather than copying the standard template.

sections.heading: KNC and the Dagan Cebu Connection
paragraphs: KNC is best known in the Philippine running community as the organiser behind Dagan Cebu — a regional race series with a loyal local following. [1] That local production experience matters: they know Cebu's roads, its permitting processes, and its running community. The flip side is that KNC hasn't yet established the kind of national reputation that draws runners from Manila or Davao in significant numbers. For Cebuano runners, this is a known quantity. For out-of-towners, it's a bet on local expertise — one that's probably worth taking given the SRP venue.

sections.heading: September Weather: What to Expect
paragraphs: September sits at the monsoon transition — the southwest monsoon (habagat) is fading and the northeast monsoon (amihan) hasn't fully arrived. [2] In Cebu, that means warm mornings (24-26°C at flag-off) climbing to 31-32°C by mid-morning, with moderate humidity and a reasonable chance of dry conditions. The SRP's coastal exposure helps — the sea breeze is a genuine cooling factor that inland Cebu courses don't get. Rain is possible but typically comes as afternoon thunderstorms; a pre-dawn start should avoid most of it. [3]

sections.heading: Should You Run It?
paragraphs: A Cebu waterfront marathon with a distinctive distance spread and a flat, fast SRP course. The pending registration is the main friction point — bookmark and monitor. If KNC delivers on the SRP's potential, this could become a fixture on the Visayas running calendar. 20 September 2026 at City Di Mare, South Road Properties, Cebu City. [1]
